Checks run:
- JSON was read in full, not parsed. A multiline Grep found no comma before a closing bracket.
- The keys match the photoreal proof script exactly.
- All 5 speakers and the location talkies_lobby exist in the bible.
- emotion_tags match the inline tags on all 27 lines. Only l06 has two tags, each on its own clause. No tag is followed by an ellipsis.

- Hand character count is 1,025 code points (nukta letters counted as two), the same as the writer's. The densest line is l15 at 10.5 characters a second; none is over 12.

Not checked:

- The projected running time (about 134 s) is an estimate fitted to the proof's measured takes.
- The vote split is my judgement: about 45 A to 55 B, inside D-004's 65/35 limit.

Why it passes:
- It opens inside the moment: the phone buzzes with Bhaiyaji's name at 1.5 s, straight after s2e02's cliffhanger.
- Stakes are concrete before the halfway mark: 'कस्बे का राशन', 'ज़िंदा', 'उसी FIR में उसका नाम'.
- Both options are costed out loud before the vote: A at l19, B at l17 and l20, plus 'उनके पास असली है'.
- The trap stays ambiguous (l12) and nothing leaks the stamped slip or the transfer.
- The question l27 is spoken low but fully voiced over a ducked bed and is not answered.
- The Hinglish sounds natural for each character, and no lines were padded.

The two must-fix items are staging only (b4 shot 2 at about 10.9 s and b6 shot 1 at about 9.1 s on single stills). Neither changes a line or the length.

must_fix: PERFORMABILITY / NATURAL ENGLISH (must fix): l26, b9, a protected key line. 'If you say so, I will go. If you say so...' collides with the common English phrase 'if you say so', which means doubtful or grudging agreement. That is especially true of the trailing form at the end of the line, the last thing Nirala says before the question. His voice note says b8 and b9 are played straight with 'no comic colour at all', and the voice model is likely to read the trailing phrase with that wry, resigned tune. The Hindi 'आप कहें तो' means 'if you tell me to'. Replacement: "[quietly] If you tell me to, I will go. If you tell me to..." Tag unchanged; target_seconds 4.2 -> 4.9; target_total_seconds 123.3 -> 124.0 (b9 action unchanged: 'l26, which he leaves unfinished' still holds). If length matters more, an equally valid version: "[quietly] Tell me to, and I will go. Tell me to..." (target stays 4.2, total unchanged). No other line changes.
